A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMNet research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original assembly experiments, transfer evaluations, ablations, and qualitative analyses on Breaking Bad and a synthetic toy dataset in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons and ablations in Tables 1-4 and A1-A5.

M1.justification: Equations (2), (3), and (10) revise the stated training losses from ungated squared margin deviations to deviations weighted by positive-part coefficients. This changes the specified objective outside the active margins. The architecture and inference procedure remain unchanged; implementation changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover volume-constrained and vanilla Breaking Bad, everyday/artifact transfer, pairwise and multi-part assembly, and the same six-pattern synthetic dataset. The added Section 4.5 footnote reiterates existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. PMTR, Jigsaw, and GeoTransformer remain in Tables 2-3; DiffAssemble and PuzzleFusion++ already appeared in Table A1 in v1. The multi-part and toy-dataset comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Sampling, dataset constraints, metrics, training budgets, model dimensions, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4.1-4.2 and Appendix C. The new footnote repeats the previously documented volume-constrained evaluation setting.

E4.justification: Tables 1 and A3-A5 retain the same component, matching-strategy, and baseline ablations. Orientation visualizations, correlation analyses, t-SNE analysis, transfer experiments, and failure cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-4 and A1-A5 and the qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains CMNet CRDs of 0.28 and 0.49 and PMTR CRDs of 0.39 and 0.60 for everyday and artifact, respectively, in the displayed units.

T1.justification: The loss definitions in Equations (2), (3), and (10) introduce clipped adaptive weights, which are not algebraically equivalent to the previous unrestricted squared deviations. The rotation-invariance definitions and proof in Appendix B.3 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about orientation alignment, identical surface matching, opposite occupancy, reduced ambiguity, and assembly performance.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes the explanation of positive-match distances from being close to the margin to falling below it, consistent with the revised weighting. Interpretations of experimental results and the limitations concerning low overlap and indistinguishable fracture surfaces remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.5 now explicitly specifies the positive and negative pair-weight calculations, improving the loss implementation specification. The repeated values Delta_p = 0.1, Delta_n = 1.4, and gamma = 24 were already disclosed in v1's Appendix C.1; hardware, training settings, and project access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 57 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning against Jigsaw's primal-dual descriptors. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the loss explanations in Section 3.1 and Appendix B.5, an added dataset reminder in a Section 4.5 footnote, and the version header. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation (2) moves from page 4 to page 3, and Figure 5 moves from the right to the left column on page 6. Text, footnote, and reference reflow produces further modest layout changes. Figure content, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised loss definitions and accompanying explanation resolve the mismatch between unrestricted squared deviations and the intended margin behavior, improving mathematical precision and reproducibility. The added footnote also reinforces the existing dataset distinction. These are limited improvements: empirical evidence and main claims are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changes or retraining occurred.
